detection_candidates.rationale: medium — the sending and lure infrastructure is off-victim (hunt/threat-intel space), but inbound email URL analysis, newly-registered-domain and lookalike-domain detection, and secure-email-gateway link detonation make the delivery observable at the perimeter
medium — scanning against internet-facing assets is detectable via perimeter/IDS and honeypot telemetry, though attribution to this actor is hard
medium — execution of Invoke-HuntSMBShares and mass share enumeration on hosts is detectable via PowerShell script-block logging, though the tools themselves are legitimate
medium — inbound link/attachment analysis, sandbox detonation, and user-reported-phish workflows make delivery detectable at the email perimeter
medium — web-proxy/DNS logging of redirect chains to lookalike domains and browser-exploit telemetry provide detection surface
medium — WAF/IPS signatures and anomalous server-process child spawns detect exploitation, though n-day/0-day can precede the first artifact

medium — highly feasible identity detection: impossible-travel, anomalous sign-ins from VPN/VPS ASNs, new-device/KMSI events and Azure AD/Entra sign-in-log analytics catch valid-account cloud abuse even when the credential itself is legitimate
medium — anomalous domain-account logon (Event ID 4624/4768) from unusual sources, and RDP/Citrix access-pattern analytics, provide detection surface
medium — use of default accounts is detectable via authentication auditing where such accounts should be dormant/disabled
medium — highly feasible: bursts of denied/repeated MFA prompts followed by an approval, and MFA-fatigue analytics in the IdP sign-in logs, are strong high-fidelity signals

detection_candidates.technique_name: Use Alternate Authentication Material: Web Session Cookie
detection_candidates.rationale: medium — anomalous session reuse, sign-ins with valid session but new device/IP, and KMSI/persistent-session anomalies are detectable in cloud sign-in logs, though stolen-cookie reuse can look legitimate
medium — feasible: app-password creation events and new legacy-auth/app-password sign-ins are auditable in Entra ID; alerting on app-password registration is a strong control
medium — web-proxy/DNS logs of clicks to newly-registered lookalike domains and browser-download telemetry provide detection
medium — double-extension LNK execution, LNK-spawned command interpreters and macro-document child processes are detectable via process-creation and EDR telemetry

medium — PowerShell script-block/module logging, AMSI, and suspicious cmdlet sequences (ExecutionPolicy change + Invoke-HuntSMBShares) are strong detections; obfuscation/AES-decrypt-in-memory reduces static visibility

detection_candidates.technique_name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Visual Basic
detection_candidates.rationale: medium — wscript/cscript executing .vbs that spawns curl/cmd, and StrReverse('llehS.tpircsW') obfuscation, are detectable via process-creation telemetry and the published NICECURL YARA rule

detection_candidates.technique_name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Windows Command Shell
detection_candidates.rationale: medium — cmd.exe spawning curl with C2 URLs, especially from a script host, is detectable via command-line process auditing
medium — WMI process-creation and WMI-Activity operational logging detect anomalous WMI execution
medium — scheduled-task creation (Event ID 4698, Sysmon) with suspicious actions/paths is a reliable detection

detection_candidates.technique_name: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder
detection_candidates.rationale: medium — Run-key writes and Startup-folder drops are classic, well-covered autostart-monitoring detections
medium — local-account creation (Event ID 4720) on servers/endpoints is a high-fidelity persistence signal

detection_candidates.technique_name: Account Manipulation: Additional Email Delegate Permissions
detection_candidates.rationale: medium — feasible: mailbox-permission and delegate-grant changes are captured in Exchange/Unified Audit logs and are strong identity-persistence signals

detection_candidates.technique_name: Account Manipulation: Additional Local or Domain Groups
detection_candidates.rationale: medium — group-membership-change auditing (Event ID 4728/4732) detects additions to privileged/RDP groups
medium — new/modified web-content files and web-server processes spawning shells are detectable via FIM and process-lineage analytics
medium — highly feasible identity detection: inbox-rule creation/modification and auto-forwarding rules are logged in Exchange/Unified Audit and are a well-known BEC/espionage signal
medium — runtime decode-then-execute is partly observable via AMSI/script-block logging of the decrypted stage
medium — 'start /MIN' and hidden-window flags in command lines are detectable via process-creation auditing
medium — registry-modification auditing (Sysmon EID 13) on autostart/config keys provides detection
medium — anomalous rundll32 command lines (odd DLLs/exports, network activity) are detectable via process/command-line analytics
medium — file-deletion telemetry and gaps around known tool paths can flag cleanup, though deletion is inherently destructive of evidence
medium — history-clearing commands/events are detectable via shell-audit and file-monitoring, though quiet by design

detection_candidates.technique_name: Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Tools
detection_candidates.rationale: medium — security-tool tampering/stop events and Defender-configuration changes are auditable via EDR self-protection and defense-health telemetry

detection_candidates.technique_name: Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Windows Event Log
detection_candidates.rationale: medium — event-log service manipulation and logging gaps/continuity breaks are detectable via log-integrity monitoring
medium — firewall-rule and profile changes are auditable via Windows Firewall logging and registry monitoring
medium — LSASS handle-access/process-access telemetry (Sysmon EID 10) and credential-guard controls provide well-established detection
medium — bulk mailbox/directory enumeration is visible in Exchange/Entra audit logs
medium — trust-enumeration commands (nltest, etc.) are detectable via command-line auditing
medium — internal scanning/share-enumeration bursts and Invoke-HuntSMBShares execution are detectable via network and PowerShell logging
medium — host-enumeration commands and scanning patterns are detectable via endpoint and network telemetry
medium — netstat-style discovery is detectable via command-line auditing, though low-signal alone
medium — standard discovery commands are detectable but low-signal on their own

detection_candidates.technique_name: System Network Configuration Discovery: Wi-Fi Discovery
detection_candidates.rationale: medium — 'netsh wlan show profile ... key=clear' is a distinctive command-line detection
medium — whoami/user-context queries are detectable but low-signal individually
medium — process enumeration and defender-presence checks are partly observable via command-line and API telemetry
medium — broad file/directory enumeration and staging activity are detectable via file-access auditing on sensitive data stores
medium — RDP logon auditing (Event ID 4624 type 10 / 4778) from unusual sources and Citrix access analytics provide detection
medium — internal file transfers of executables/scripts (SMB/admin shares) are detectable via file-share and EDR telemetry
medium — bulk local/cloud file access and staging are detectable via data-access auditing on sensitive repositories
medium — anomalous mass mailbox access and export are detectable via Exchange/Unified Audit logs
medium — access to and copying of Outlook data files is detectable via file-access monitoring
medium — abnormal remote mailbox-access volumes and EWS/Graph access patterns are detectable via cloud mailbox audit logs

detection_candidates.technique_name: Archive Collected Data: Archive via Utility
detection_candidates.rationale: medium — 7-Zip/archive-utility execution creating large password-protected archives in staging paths is detectable via process and file telemetry
medium — curl-based beaconing from script hosts and anomalous HTTP(S) to newly-seen domains are detectable via proxy/network telemetry and process-network correlation
medium — protocol-anomaly and beacon-timing analytics provide detection surface
medium — curl/Wget/PowerShell downloads from script hosts to newly-seen domains, followed by execution, are detectable via process-network correlation
medium — protocol-on-non-standard-port analytics (e.g. TLS/HTTP on unusual ports) provide detection
medium — large uploads/downloads to a non-corporate OneDrive/outlook.com destination and anomalous cloud data-movement are detectable via CASB/cloud DLP and audit logs
medium — mass file-modification/encryption behavior and unexpected BitLocker/encryption activity are detectable via EDR ransomware behavior analytics

hunting_candidates.technique_name: Gather Victim Identity Information: Email Addresses

low — credential collection happens on attacker-controlled harvesting pages off-victim; the downstream reuse is where detection becomes feasible (see T1078)
low — off-victim OSINT reconnaissance; not detectable in defender telemetry

hunting_candidates.technique_name: Gather Victim Org Information: Determine Physical Locations
hunting_candidates.rationale: low — off-victim reconnaissance

hunting_candidates.technique_name: Gather Victim Network Information: IP Addresses
hunting_candidates.rationale: low — off-victim; beacon callbacks are only faintly observable at the mail-render stage
low — largely off-victim; on-host defender-presence checks are covered under T1518-style behavior in TAMECAT
low — persona creation is entirely off-victim; a HUNT/attribution artifact (persona-infrastructure tracking, avatar reuse, cross-platform linkage), not a host or log detection
low — account creation is off-victim; the exfil-mailbox naming pattern is a hunt indicator visible only once exfiltration occurs

low — domain registration is off-victim; a HUNT signal via newly-registered-domain feeds, registrar/hosting pivots and naming-pattern clustering rather than a host detection

low — off-victim acquisition; on-victim the resulting traffic to legitimate cloud services is hard to distinguish (see T1102.002). A hunt for anomalous glitch.me/tebi.io connections is the practical angle
low — off-victim; hunt via passive-DNS and hosting-pivot analysis
low — delivery over third-party services is largely outside enterprise email/network visibility; user-awareness and reported-contact reporting are the main levers (hunt/awareness)

hunting_candidates.technique_name: Masquerading: Match Legitimate Name or Location
hunting_candidates.rationale: low — name/location masquerade defeats name-based trust; a HUNT via double-extension detection, signer/metadata mismatch and lookalike-domain analysis rather than a single signature
low — masqueraded task/service names evade name-based review; hunt via task/service action-vs-name inconsistency
low — name-approximation defeats name-based allow-listing; hunt via account-creation review and naming-anomaly analytics

hunting_candidates.technique_name: Obfuscated Files or Information: Encrypted/Encoded File
hunting_candidates.rationale: low — encryption/encoding defeats static inspection; hunt via entropy analysis, AMSI-visible decrypted content and the published YARA constants rather than log detection

hunting_candidates.technique_name: Obfuscated Files or Information: Command Obfuscation
hunting_candidates.rationale: low — command obfuscation is designed to defeat static signatures; hunt via de-obfuscated script-block logging and behavioral analysis
low — user-mode keylogging via API hooks leaves limited telemetry; hunt via behavioral hook/injection detection

hunting_candidates.rationale: low — connectivity checks blend with normal traffic; low-signal
